title: Distributed token-window sentinel and ingress saturation predictor for private deployments
creator: Marisol Gomez
description: We need a lightweight, distributed probe that predicts ingress saturation and token-window exhaustion across Private (VPC) workers. Current probes surface high-level token throughput and latency but lack an efficient sliding-window sentinel that correlates short-term token bursts with per-worker KV cache pressure and queueing latency. This ticket delivers a probe + terraform wiring that can be deployed as a sidecar or a DaemonSet to produce aligned SLO metrics (p99/p50 latency, 5m error-rate, short-window token throughput, per-worker saturation score) and a simple alerting predictor for imminent saturation.
background: Private clusters receive variable traffic bursts from customer routes. We've observed incidents where token throughput spikes over a short window cause KV cache churn and backend queueing, producing tail latency regressions. Existing SLOs are aggregated and delayed; runbooks rely on manual verification of dashboards. We want an automated predictor that yields a 'saturation imminence' signal (0-1) with a few minutes lead time and ties to concrete mitigations (scale-up, drop to fallback model, enable request queue shedding).
proposal: Implement a distributed sliding-window sentinel that emits these metrics per worker and per-route: 1) short_window_tokens (rolling 30s/60s windows), 2) kv_cache_churn_rate (evictions/sec), 3) local_request_queue_depth, 4) p50/p95/p99 generation latency, 5) recent_error_rate (5m). Use a simple logistic predictor trained on historical telemetry to estimate saturation_imminence (stringified float 0-1). Expose metrics to Prometheus and an aggregated SLO pipeline. Deploy as a lightweight sidecar with a Terraform module and a Helm flag for Private operator. Provide a canary rollout strategy and automatic alert thresholds that map to scaling or fallback policies in the routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Per-worker metrics emitted at 10s cadence and scraped by existing prometheus job
Saturation_imminence metric documented and tested to correlate with 5x token bursts in replay tests
Terraform module exposes toggles for sidecar vs daemonset and RBAC bindings
End-to-end test: injected synthetic burst causes predictor to raise >0.7 and an automated canary policy scales a small fleet or triggers fallback
Runbook updated with playbook steps and SLAs for false positives/negatives
implementation_plan: Design proto agent: Go service with 2 collectors (token window, KV cache metrics) and simple logistic estimator (weights in config)
Add metrics & labels: cluster_id, worker_id, route_id, model_variant, quant_profile
Write Helm chart hooks and Terraform module (private-probe) that wires service account, metrics endpoint, and scrape annotations
Create e2e replay harness using staging traces to validate predictor thresholds
Integrate with alerting: pager thresholds and Console alert mappings
Document rollout plan and migrate 2 pilot customers' clusters
telemetry_and_dashboarding: Create a dedicated dashboard showing short_window_tokens, kv_cache_churn_rate, local_queue_depth, p50/p95/p99, and saturation_imminence. Add delta charts that compare predicted vs actual saturation events for the last 72h. Add a per-route table with mitigation action suggestions (scale, fallback, shed).
runbook_notes: If saturation_imminence > 0.8: check worker queue depth and KV eviction rate; if both are above configured thresholds, trigger temporary fallback routing and notify infra. False positives: lower logistic weight on short_window_tokens; false negatives: increase sensitivity or expand window. Include step-by-step terraform rollback commands and link to canary runbook. Ensure KMS keys for probe configs are available for Private deployments.
